comment: Mesh HITL bench catalog (docs/design/mesh-hitl-rig.md §10). NOT DEPLOYED YET: the bench host (a NanoPi-class SBC, question Q1) has no sbc-deploy board target, and every board serial below is a placeholder (00:00:00:00:C6:0n for the C6 DUTs, 00:00:00:00:F4:0n for the P4 boards, SERIAL_* for the instruments) that the assembly checklist (§12 step 9) replaces with the real USB serials. One composite, pin_only unit: the RP2350 RF controller, four TinyC6 u.FL DUTs on the conducted RF matrix, two P4+C6 boards, the overhead camera and the 16-channel analyser, reserved atomically (the timing measurement needs all of them at once, and nothing else may touch the conducted DUTs). Per-DUT env follows the c6-sdr convention: HITL_TTY / HITL_ADAPTER_SERIAL for DUT 0 and the _N suffix for DUT N, so the toolbox's --dut N works unchanged. The instruments are addressed by HITL_RFCTL_TTY, HITL_CAMERA_DEV and HITL_LA_DRIVER; HITL_LA_MAP names what each analyser channel taps (a DUT strip, or the controller's SYNC line) and HITL_MESHBENCH_LAYOUT_JSON is the camera's ROI layout (§7.4), both filled at assembly.

components.comment: TinyC6 u.FL DUT 0: conducted node 0 of the RF matrix (its u.FL -> pigtail -> node 0 splitter). Strips on GPIO20 (ch0) and GPIO14 (ch1), tapped by analyser D0 and D1.
components.name: c6-0

components.comment: TinyC6 u.FL DUT 1: conducted node 1 of the RF matrix (its u.FL -> pigtail -> node 1 splitter). Strips on GPIO20 (ch0) and GPIO14 (ch1), tapped by analyser D2 and D3.
components.name: c6-1

components.comment: TinyC6 u.FL DUT 2: conducted node 2 of the RF matrix (its u.FL -> pigtail -> node 2 splitter). Strips on GPIO20 (ch0) and GPIO14 (ch1), tapped by analyser D4 and D5.
components.name: c6-2

components.comment: TinyC6 u.FL DUT 3: conducted node 3 of the RF matrix (its u.FL -> pigtail -> node 3 splitter). Strips on GPIO20 (ch0) and GPIO14 (ch1), tapped by analyser D6 and D7.
components.name: c6-3

components.comment: P4+C6 board 0 (DUT 4): the P4's USB-Serial-JTAG (flash/monitor the P4; the P4 reflashes its C6, firmware/p4/c6flash). Over the air, not conducted, unless its C6 has an antenna connector (question Q3). Two strips per board today (PARLIO lanes on GPIO20/21), sixteen once the 16-lane encoder lands; analyser D8 taps lane 0.
components.name: p4-0

components.comment: P4+C6 board 1 (DUT 5): the P4's USB-Serial-JTAG (flash/monitor the P4; the P4 reflashes its C6, firmware/p4/c6flash). Over the air, not conducted, unless its C6 has an antenna connector (question Q3). Two strips per board today (PARLIO lanes on GPIO20/21), sixteen once the 16-lane encoder lands; analyser D9 taps lane 0.
components.name: p4-1

components.comment: The RP2350 (Pico 2) RF controller running pi/hitl/meshbench/rfctl (USB CDC, product 'rfctl mesh-bench'). Drives every switch and attenuator of the matrix through the 74HC595 chain, toggles SYNC (analyser D12) on each commit, and timestamps frame starts on its FSTI inputs.
components.name: rfctl-0

components.comment: Overhead global-shutter UVC camera (§7.1), MJPEG at 120 fps. HITL_MESHBENCH_LAYOUT_JSON (strips + syncled ROI boxes) is written once at assembly with `mesh_bench --calibrate-layout`.
components.name: cam-0

components.comment: 16-channel logic analyser (DSLogic Plus class, sigrok driver dreamsourcelab-dslogic). Raw USB, no tty: like the c6-sdr HackRF it needs the privileged single-unit environment. Channel map: D0-D7 = c6-0..3 strips 0/1, D8-D9 = p4-0/p4-1 lane 0, D10-D11 = p4-0 lanes 1 and 15 (lane skew), D12 = controller SYNC, D13-D15 spare.
components.name: la-0

units.comment: The whole bench as one atomic, pin_only unit (the c6-sdr pattern): reachable only by name or by type mesh-bench, so caps-only netstack jobs can never land on the conducted DUTs. Reserve with `--unit mesh-bench-1` or `--type mesh-bench`.
units.name: mesh-bench-1
